label: SYNTHETIC DEVELOPMENT FIXTURE - two candidates that both pass the mock gate against the same baseline; scripted mock outputs, not model outputs or measurements

hypotheses.claim: Advancing the progress checkpoint before durably writing the index record lets a crash between the two operations silently drop that record on restart.
hypotheses.mechanism: On restart the indexer resumes after the checkpointed note, so a note whose record was never appended is skipped.
hypotheses.falsifier: If a crash injected between the checkpoint write and the index append, followed by restart, still yields every note indexed exactly once, the hypothesis is false.

hypotheses.claim: Replaying a note after restart may duplicate its index record because the append is not idempotent.
hypotheses.mechanism: A crash after the append but before the checkpoint causes the note to be processed again.
hypotheses.falsifier: If a crash after the append followed by restart never produces duplicate records, the hypothesis is false.

candidates.title: Make output durable before advancing progress
candidates.procedure: For resumable work: (1) write and flush the output for an item; (2) only then advance the progress checkpoint; (3) make reprocessing an item idempotent (for example a keyed upsert) so a crash between the steps is safe to retry.
candidates.known_limits: Does not cover side effects that cannot be rolled back or deduplicated. Does not prescribe a global lock.

candidates.title: Make reprocessing an item idempotent
candidates.procedure: For resumable work that may replay an item after a crash: write each output with a stable item key (for example a keyed upsert or a per-item file named by the key) so that processing the same item twice leaves exactly one record.
candidates.known_limits: Does not prevent lost items when progress is advanced before output is durable.

1.title: Crash between checkpoint write and index append
1.intervention: terminate the process after checkpoint.json is written and before index.jsonl is appended, then restart
1.expected_invariant: after restart every note is indexed exactly once
1.reference_impl: append record; flush; then advance checkpoint (fixture text only)
1.faulty_impl: advance checkpoint; then append record (fixture text only)
1.oracle: compare the set and multiplicity of indexed note ids with the input note ids (fixture text only)

2.title: Duplicate record after replay
2.intervention: terminate after append and before checkpoint, then restart
2.oracle: count records per note id (fixture text only)
